module_role: Mainstream DDR5 SDRAM memory (JESD79-5): a parallel, source-synchronous, double-data-rate DRAM whose DIMM is split into two independent 32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels, each driven over CA[13:0] + CS_n (2-cycle commands) and CK_t/CK_c with DQ[31:0] on DQS_t/DQS_c. The device provides DFE on DQ, on-die ECC, 32 banks / 8 bank groups with same-bank refresh, BL16, internal VrefDQ/VrefCA with training, and an expanded mode-register space; the module adds a PMIC, SPD hub, and (RDIMM) RCD.

integration_overview.interconnect: TSV + microbump within the stack; 2.5D silicon interposer to the host SoC.
integration_overview.host_role: memory controller + PHY is bus master for all channels
integration_overview.dram_role: stack is the target; per-channel independent command decode
integration_overview.physical_proximity: interposer keeps memory close to the host

interface_categories: Command/address interface — CA[13:0] + CS_n (2-cycle commands) per sub-channel.
Clock interface — differential CK_t/CK_c per sub-channel.
Data interface — DQ[31:0] + DQS_t/DQS_c (32 bits, 40 with ECC) per sub-channel.
Module interface — PMIC (power), SPD hub (config), RCD (RDIMM clock/CA buffering).
interconnect_topologies_supported: Multiple ranks per sub-channel addressed by CS_n.
default_signal_values_when_omitted: Banks precharged (IDLE); CKE high; DQ tri-stated between bursts; refresh (REFab/REFsb) issued within tREFI.
soc_dependent_items: Memory-controller scheduling of the two independent sub-channels.
Selected speed bin (DDR5-3200 .. DDR5-8400) and timing parameters.
Device organization (x4 / x8 / x16) and module type (U/SO/R/LR-DIMM).
Training schedule (CA / write-leveling / read / write, DFE, VrefDQ/VrefCA, ZQ).
PMIC / SPD-hub / RCD configuration over the sideband bus.

low_power_modes.power_down: Per-channel power-down with fast exit; clock may be gated.
low_power_modes.self_refresh: DRAM self-refreshes; channel clock may stop; exit re-synchronizes.

compatibility_notes: HBM3 keeps the 1024-bit interface of prior HBM generations but doubles channels (16 x 64-bit vs 8 x 128-bit). HBM4 (JESD270-4, April 2025) widens to 2048 bits and is backwards compatible with HBM3 controllers, but is a separate standard out of scope of JESD238.

system_examples.detail: Industry-first HBM3; up to 819 GB/s per stack; multiple HBM3 sites (e.g. five active sites = 80 GB and ~3 TB/s; 16 GB / 600 GB/s per site).
12-Hi 24 GB stacks aggregated for multi-TB/s (e.g. ~4.9 TB/s with six 24 GB stacks).

topology_description: DIMM -> two independent sub-channels -> bank groups -> banks. Each sub-channel is 32 data bits (40 with ECC) with its own CA bus, CS_n, and clock. RDIMMs interpose a Registering Clock Driver (RCD) on CK/CA; LRDIMMs add data buffers (DB). An on-module PMIC supplies 1.1 V / 1.8 V and an SPD hub holds configuration.
device_classes_examples: DDR5 UDIMM / SODIMM (desktop / laptop main memory)
